For each valid position `(b,t)` with nonzero `sequence[b,t]` and `positive[b,t]`, extract history only from `sequence[b,:t+1]`; the target is `positive[b,t]`, with `negative[b,t]` its paired negative. Never append the target or later sequence entries. Example: sequence `[0,a,b,c]`, positives `[0,b,c,d]` gives prefixes `[a]→b`, `[a,b]→c`, `[a,b,c]→d`. This follows the [original sampler’s shifted-target construction](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py).

For independent attribution, right-align each prefix in a zero-padded length-L tensor, perturb only its observed history, and recompute baseline and perturbed features in evaluation mode. Use the actual adapter’s `log2feats` and `predict_score`, preserving its scoring head. Select the final nonpadding feature: index `L−1` for nonempty right-aligned prefixes; generally, use the greatest nonzero index, not `nonzero_count−1`. Verify causal attention blocks keys after each query and preserves the architecture’s padding behavior. Crucial distinction: repacking a prefix changes absolute positional embeddings. Thus independent right-aligned scores need not equal the original training feature at position t. To attribute that exact training prediction, preserve original positions, clear the suffix, and score feature t. These implications follow from the [implementation’s positional embeddings, causal mask, and final-feature scoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/master/python/model.py).

The supplied local contract yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, so user identity is unavailable from that tuple. Preserve `(category,user_id,position)` through a diagnostic sidecar or construct diagnostic examples directly from `view.user_train`; shuffled batch indices or matching histories cannot reliably identify users. Aggregate prefix effects within each identified user before averaging users.
